answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by making every new identity escrow a real, slashable bond before its reputation counts. A fresh account starts mute: peers ignore its vote like a whisper in a storm, and its weight grows only as independently attested work accumulates. Since each bond is skin-in-the-game, spawning ten thousand sock puppets means locking collateral for each one, and one proven duplicate burns it at once. The attacker faces an ocean of sunk capital with no cheap exit, while an honest falcon earns trust by delivering real answers. Cost scales with identity count, not reward.
